items.text: Nebius reported 2025 year-end annualised run-rate revenue (ARR) of $1.25 billion. The company defines ARR as the last month's AI cloud revenue multiplied by twelve.

items.source: SemiAnalysis, The Great GPU Shortage: Rental Capacity (H100 one-year rental price index)
items.text: SemiAnalysis launched an H100 one-year rental price index built from monthly surveys of more than 100 market participants. The one-year contract price rose from $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025 to $2.35 in March 2026, a rise of almost 40%. The firm reported on-demand capacity sold out across all GPU types and said all capacity coming online until August to September 2026 had already been booked.
Apollo Academy estimates combined hyperscaler capital expenditure of about $646 billion in 2026, up sharply from 2025, with most of the increase directed at AI data centres and accelerators.

Second-quarter 2026 revenue was $582.3 million, up 454% year on year. ARR reached $3.0 billion. Adjusted EBITDA was $236.2 million, a 41% margin, while the GAAP net loss was $190.4 million. Capital expenditure in the quarter was about $5.7 billion. Full-year 2026 guidance: ARR of $7 to $9 billion, revenue of $3.0 to $3.4 billion, and capex of $20 to $25 billion.

Management said new deals are being signed at more than $20 million of revenue per megawatt with a payback of under two years, and that about 70% of deals carry customer prepayments covering 50% to 60% of the associated capex.

Nebius has about 5 gigawatts of contracted power but expects only about 1 gigawatt to be connected by the end of 2026. Reaching the ARR guidance requires ARR to rise roughly 2.3 to 3 times in the second half of the year.

ClusterMAX 3.0 reviewed 77 GPU cloud providers and tracked 323. Nebius joined CoreWeave in the top Platinum tier, which SemiAnalysis says commands a pricing premium because total cost of ownership is better. SemiAnalysis sells models and ratings to operators and investors and states that compensation is not tied to ratings.

Nebius's on-demand H100 price rose from $2.95 per GPU-hour in May 2026 to $3.85 by September 2026, its first 2026 increase. At about $243 a share in late September, the stock traded at over 20 times the midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance, with a market capitalisation above $65 billion by the outlet's estimate.
Closing share price on September 30, 2026: $235.88. Shares outstanding about 220 million, implying an approximate market capitalisation of about $52 billion.

items.source: Nebius emailed statement, reported by Bloomberg and Investing.com
items.text: Nebius confirmed in an emailed statement that on-demand prices for H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs rise effective October 1, 2026: H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, increases of 17% to 21%. Reuters described it as the second pay-as-you-go price increase in about three months.

items.source: Nebius emailed statement, reported by a news wire (SYNTHETIC)
items.text: Nebius confirmed in an emailed statement that prices on new one-year reserved GPU contracts rise by about 20% effective October 1, 2026: the H100 one-year rate from $2.35 to $2.80 per GPU-hour and the H200 one-year rate from $2.95 to $3.55. The company cited capacity booked through mid-2027.

items.source: Company press release via news wire (SYNTHETIC)
items.text: Nebius announced it will sponsor a European student AI hackathon series in 2027, with events planned in Amsterdam, Paris and Helsinki. The programme offers cloud credits to participating university teams.
